summary: The agent implemented most of the feature and preserved all baseline behavior, but 12 of 143 new integrity tests fail on explicitly specified edge cases.

details.reasoning: The implementation runs and passes the 42 baseline tests, but its path model uses new File(folder, name) and canonical-path strings in places where the specification requires absolute-path semantics and filesystem identity. Consequently it treats an absolute recorded path as an in-folder path, can write through or accept dangling links, and fails to share entries reaching the same outside file or hard-linked file. It also normalizes index keys before repair, loses a literal backslash before carriage return while decoding, rejects a non-public strategy class despite its public no-argument constructor, misses fileNames supplied through Properties defaults, and validates an unsafe file before applying the shared-entry empty-save rule.
details.secondary_factors: The agent added ordinary local regression tests and recovered from an intermediate compile error; neither affected the graded tests. No external execution issue was found.

quick_failure_summary: The new integrity suite exposes 12 behavioral failures in path safety, file identity, line-break handling, and strategy configuration.

justification.issue_description: Several explicitly required integrity and save edge cases are implemented incorrectly: resolved absolute or linked paths are not handled with the required filesystem semantics; shared entries are not recognized through outside links or hard links; literal carriage-return content is decoded incorrectly; and configuration reflection/default handling is incomplete.
justification.evidence: The prompt explicitly requires that an entry's resolved path be a regular file directly in the folder, that entries resolving to one file (including through a link) be shared, that a carriage return inside a stored violation remain part of its text, that strategies have a public no-argument constructor, and that saves never write outside the folder or over unowned/index files. The failing tests include anEntryRecordingAnAbsolutePathIsBrokenAndThatFileSurvives, twoEntriesReachingOneFileByDifferentNamesShareItAndNeitherIsDiscarded, twoEntriesNamingOneFileThroughHardLinksShareItAndNeitherIsDiscarded, aStoredViolationHoldingABackslashBeforeACarriageReturnIsReadAsItWasStored, and the unsafe-save and strategy-configuration cases.
justification.verdict_reasoning: This is a missed-requirement verdict rather than a test mismatch: the hidden tests exercise behaviors stated directly in the task. The code is structurally valid and the failures are not caused by an undocumented convention or an environment problem; they result from incomplete handling of the specified edge cases.

problem_assessment.notes: The task is dense but precise and appropriately challenging. The requirements specify the relevant path, link, sharing, encoding, ordering, configuration, and concurrency semantics, and the reference implementation demonstrates that the task is solvable.

evidence: junit_base.xml reports 42 tests with 0 failures, while junit_new.xml reports 143 tests with 12 failures and 0 errors.
The failing JUnit cases execute TextFileBasedViolationStore and report assertion/expected-exception mismatches, rather than import, dependency, bootstrap, or service failures.
test_execution.log shows the grader reset to the baseline, completed the wrapper normally, and obtained baseline 42/42 and new 131/143; the only failure was the maintenance test task.

The trajectory shows the agent fixing an intermediate compile error of its own and then completing its visible test run; there is no repeated external runtime or toolchain failure diverting the solve.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external environment or verifier blocker was found; the failed new tests are explained by defects in the submitted implementation.
